name: BMI088
title: BMI088: 6-axis IMU, 16-bit triaxial accelerometer (±3 to ±24 g) and triaxial gyroscope (±125 to ±2000 °/s), SPI and I²C, LGA-16
summary: A six-degree-of-freedom inertial unit in a 3.0 × 4.5 × 0.95 mm LGA: a three-axis 16-bit accelerometer with ranges of ±3, ±6, ±12 and ±24 g and a three-axis 16-bit gyroscope with ranges of ±125 to ±2000 °/s, plus an 11-bit temperature reading. It is aimed at drones and robots, where board and frame resonances above a few hundred hertz have to be rejected. The two sensors are separate devices behind one set of pins, each with its own register map, chip select or I²C address, interrupt pins and FIFO (1024 bytes for the accelerometer, 100 frames for the gyroscope). The core runs from 2.4 to 3.6 V on VDD and the interface from 1.2 to 3.6 V on VDDIO; it leaves the factory calibrated.
key_figures: accelerometer 150 µA typ; gyroscope 5 mA typ
SPI up to 10 MHz; I²C up to 400 kHz

circuits.title: SPI connection
circuits.description: The part on a 4-wire SPI bus. PS and the NC pin go to ground, which puts the gyroscope on SPI; the accelerometer follows after the first rising edge on its chip select CSB1. Both data outputs, SDO1 and SDO2, join the one MISO line, and the host picks a sensor with CSB_ACCEL or CSB_GYRO. VDD and VDDIO each have a 100 nF capacitor to ground, and the two grounds are joined. The four interrupt lines go to the host.

circuits.title: I²C connection
circuits.description: The part on an I²C bus. PS and CSB1 go to VDDIO, putting both sensors on I²C, and CSB2 is left floating. SDO1 and SDO2 become the address inputs A0_ACCEL and A0_GYRO: low gives 0x18 and 0x68, high gives 0x19 and 0x69. The NC pin goes to ground; VDD and VDDIO each have a 100 nF capacitor to ground. SCL and SDA are pulled up to VDDIO by external resistors. The four interrupt lines go to the host.

operation.text: The accelerometer and the gyroscope behave as two separate slaves sharing SCK/SCL and SDI/SDA. Each has its own register map, reached by its own chip select (CSB1 for the accelerometer, CSB2 for the gyroscope) or its own I²C address, and its own data output, interrupt pins and FIFO. They can be used one at a time or together, with their data synchronised.

The bus is fixed by hardware. The gyroscope reads the PS pin: ground means SPI, VDDIO means I²C. The accelerometer always wakes in I²C mode and changes to SPI on the first rising edge it sees on CSB1, staying there until the next power-on reset; a throwaway SPI read (of ACC_CHIP_ID, for example, whose result is not valid) is enough to make that edge. Setting the two sensors to different interfaces is not advised, since they share pins.
After power-on reset the gyroscope is already in normal mode and the accelerometer is in suspend. To start the accelerometer: apply power, wait 1 ms, write 4 to ACC_PWR_CTRL (0x7D), then wait 450 µs.

VDD feeds the internal blocks and VDDIO mostly the interface. Either may sit anywhere in its own range regardless of the other, and either can be switched off while the other stays on. While VDDIO is off, CSB, SDI, SCK and PS have to stay close to GNDIO. A power-on reset clears the logic and all registers, so every non-default setting has to be written again; it also resets the interface choice.

ACC_PWR_CTRL turns both the accelerometer and its temperature sensor on or off: 0x04 for normal mode, 0x00 for suspend. The part sits in suspend after any reset and needs up to 1 ms to boot after a power-on or soft reset, so it must be switched on before it gives acceleration data. ACC_PWR_CONF (0x7C) holds 0x03 for suspend and 0x00 for active.

Normal mode samples continuously and is the state after power-up. Suspend (0x80 to GYRO_LPM1) powers down the analog section and stops sampling but keeps the last rate data and every configuration register readable. Deep suspend (0x20 to GYRO_LPM1) keeps only the interface alive and loses the configuration, so settings must be rewritten afterwards. Writing 0x00 or a soft reset returns to normal; moving directly between suspend and deep suspend is not allowed. Any reset or mode change takes up to 30 ms, during which the gyroscope should not be accessed. Consecutive writes need a pause between them.

Sensor data are 16-bit two's complement (11-bit for temperature), each split into a low and a high byte. Read the low byte first: that latches the matching high byte so the two belong to one sample. A burst read increments the address after each byte and holds all data registers of that sensor for as long as it lasts, so one burst gives X, Y and Z from the same sample.

The digital low-pass filter's corner follows the output data rate and the oversampling setting chosen in ACC_CONF: normal, 2-fold (OSR2) or 4-fold (OSR4). ODR runs from 12.5 to 1600 Hz; the corner frequencies are in the cut-off table.
GYRO_BANDWIDTH picks one of eight pairs of output data rate (100 to 2000 Hz) and filter bandwidth (12 to 532 Hz).

Electrostatic force deflects the proof mass, which exercises the whole signal chain and shows as a fixed offset added to whatever acceleration is present, so the test is run with the part held still. Sequence: write 0x03 to ACC_RANGE (±24 g); write 0xA7 to ACC_CONF (1.6 kHz, normal mode, continuous filter); wait over 2 ms; write 0x0D to ACC_SELF_TEST for positive polarity; wait over 50 ms and read all three axes; write 0x09 for negative polarity; wait over 50 ms and read again; write 0x00 to end the test; compare the positive-minus-negative difference with the minimum table; wait over 50 ms before normal use. A reset afterwards is advised because the test disturbs the interrupt logic; without one, disable the interrupts, change their settings, wait at least 50 ms and enable them again.

This test does not move the MEMS structure. Write 1 to trig_bist in GYRO_SELF_TEST; when bist_rdy goes to 1 the result is in bist_fail (0 pass, 1 fail). Bit 4, rate_ok, reports a check that runs continuously in the background and reads 1 when the sensor is working.

The accelerometer flags new data in bit 7 of ACC_INT_STAT_1 and can route it to INT1 and/or INT2 through INT1_INT2_MAP_DATA; the pins' drive and polarity are set in INT1_IO_CONF and INT2_IO_CONF. The gyroscope's new-data interrupt fires after each new Z-axis sample, must first be enabled with 0x80 in GYRO_INT_CTRL, clears itself after 280 to 400 µs, and is routed to INT3 and/or INT4 through INT3_INT4_IO_MAP, with pin behaviour set in INT3_INT4_IO_CONF.

Writing 0xB6 to ACC_SOFTRESET or GYRO_SOFTRESET acts much like a power cycle of that sensor: after a delay (1 ms for the accelerometer, 30 ms for the gyroscope) every setting returns to its default. It works from any mode but must not be sent while NVM is being written. On I²C the accelerometer takes the reset at the SCL rising edge of the ACK bit and carries it out 0.5 to 1 µs later when advanced power save is off; SDA is released at once, whatever SCL is doing. A host that needs a proper ACK for the reset write must first enable advanced power save and disable the sensor and the auxiliary interface.
Both sensors have a FIFO with two modes: FIFO (stop when full) and STREAM (overwrite the oldest data when full). Each can raise a watermark interrupt at a set fill level and a full interrupt.

1024 bytes, holding frames that each start with a header byte. Enable it with bit 6 of FIFO_CONFIG_1 (0x49); bit 0 of FIFO_CONFIG_0 (0x48) picks STREAM (0, default) or FIFO (1). It fills at the ODR, or slower by 2^k with k from 0 to 7 in FIFO_DOWNS. INT1 or INT2 set as inputs can be recorded as tag bits in each data frame header. A skip frame reports overflowed frames, a sensortime frame appears when the FIFO runs empty during a burst read, an input-config frame marks a range or filter change, and a drop frame stands in for a sample lost to reconfiguration. A partly read frame is sent again whole next time unless an overflow intervenes; reading past the end returns 0x8000. The full interrupt comes when only room for two more frames remains; the watermark interrupt when the byte count reaches FIFO_WTM. Both are routed by INT1_INT2_MAP_DATA and held off while FIFO_DATA is being read; a latched one clears once the status is read and the level is below the threshold. FIFO_LENGTH gives the 14-bit byte count; 0xB0 to ACC_SOFTRESET resets the FIFO. FIFO_DATA must be read as a burst; its address does not increment.

Up to 100 frames, each holding X, Y and Z rate (6 bytes), enabled by choosing a mode in FIFO_CONFIG_1 (0x3E) and filled at the ODR. Read it by burst from FIFO_DATA (0x3F); a frame cut short is lost and the next read starts at a frame boundary. FIFO_STATUS gives the frame count and an overrun flag that clears only on a write to the FIFO configuration. Full interrupt: at 100 frames in FIFO mode, 99 in STREAM mode. Watermark interrupt: at the level in FIFO_CONFIG_0 (0x3D), and writing that register empties the FIFO. At 400 kHz I²C every filter setting can be used; at 200 kHz, rates of 1 kHz and below; at 100 kHz, 400 Hz and below.

One of INT3 or INT4 (not both) can be made an input that tags FIFO data, for example for image and video stabilisation. Bit 5 of FIFO_EXT_INT_S (0x34) turns the mode on and bit 4 picks the pin. The Z-axis LSB then serves as the tag: while the pin is high each new FIFO word carries a 1, and after it falls one more word may still be tagged before the bit returns to 0. The other 15 Z bits keep their meaning, and the tag's time resolution equals the ODR.

Registers are 8 bits wide in an 8-bit address space, one map per sensor. Reserved registers are to be ignored. After a write, wait at least 2 µs in normal mode or 1000 µs in suspend mode before the next one; the I²C timing gives tIDLE_wacc_sum as 450 µs minimum.

Modes 00 and 11 are both accepted; the part chooses by the level of SCK when CSB falls. Each transfer is 16 bits: bit 0 is read (1) or write (0), bits 1 to 7 the register address, and bits 8 to 15 the data. The part shifts data out as SCK falls and the host samples them as SCK rises. Holding CSB low continues a burst read with the address incrementing. The accelerometer differs on reads: it first sends one byte of no meaning, so a single register takes a 2-byte read and the six acceleration bytes take a 7-byte read from 0x12 with the first byte thrown away. The gyroscope sends no such byte.

Standard and fast mode with 7-bit addressing; SCL and SDA need pull-ups to VDDIO. A write is START, address with R/W = 0, register address, data byte, STOP, each byte acknowledged by the part. A read writes the register address, then a repeated START and the address with R/W = 1; the master acknowledges each byte and ends with a NACK and STOP. The address increments through a multi-byte read, and each new read starts from the last address written (0x00 by default). A START followed at once by a STOP, with no SCL clock between, is not recognised.

Acceleration or rotation along the marked axes gives positive output. At rest, an axis reads +1 g when gravity points opposite to it: lying flat with the top face up the part reads 0 g on X and Y and +1 g on Z, and the gyroscope reads 0 °/s on all axes.
Keep the top copper layer under the part free of vias, traces and other metal. Land pattern tolerances are those of the package drawing.

The MEMS element survives shocks of several thousand g, but a hammer blow on or near the part, or a drop onto a hard surface, can go beyond that. ESD protection of 2 kV HBM is built in; normal CMOS precautions still apply. Every terminal must stay within the supply range for correct operation, and no unused input may float; unused INT pins are left unconnected. The part is RoHS compliant and halogen free.
